method.name: Horn (1981) 3x3 weighted finite difference on true 3D pixel-centre positions
method.neighbourhood: 3 x 3 DEM pixels (weights 1-2-1); centre pixel height not used
method.horizontal: true ground distances: pixel centres placed at (1737.4 km + h) x exact inverse stereographic unit vector, so the projection scale k = 2/(1+sin|lat|) and the terrain radius are included
method.vertical_reference: local lunar horizontal at each pixel = plane normal to that pixel's radial unit vector (sphere); symmetric differences cancel curvature, so curvature is not counted as slope
method.heights: DN x 0.5 m at pixel centres (no interpolation, no render mesh, no shading normals)
method.invalid: a cell is invalid if any 3x3 neighbour is outside the raster or nodata (LOLA LDEMs have no nodata value)
method.percentiles: nearest rank on stored values: value at rank ceil(p/100 * n) of the sorted valid cells
method.exceedance: stored slope strictly greater than the threshold (equal is not an exceedance), threshold at 0.01 deg
method.area_weighting: equal-area: planimetric pixel area (s/k)^2 varies by a factor 1.0000053 within the footprint; weighted and unweighted exceedance differ by at most 9.81e-08
method.scale_note: Each value is the slope of a 20 m DEM cell measured across about 40 m. It is not a slope at a smaller scale: boulders, small craters, the lander footprint and local roughness are not resolved, and the DEM is interpolated where no laser shot fell.

footprint.centre: the site coordinate (vertical of the modeled observer)
footprint.distance: great-circle ground distance on the 1737.4 km sphere between pixel centres and the site unit vector
footprint.halo: the 3x3 stencil reads one pixel beyond the footprint; every footprint stencil lies inside the raster

observer_cell.note: slope of the DEM cell containing the site coordinate (20 m cell, about 40 m baseline)

shot_quality.note: LDEC_80S_20M counts; a quality indicator for the interpolated DEM, not an accuracy guarantee

mapping.note: affine fit of renderer-frame (x, z) of every grid pixel centre to its cell indices
